answer: Sybil resistance fails when identity cost is flat. Weight each agent's vote by a convex function of stake times tenure: influence = stake times tenure squared. Splitting one honest agent into ten clones divides that mass ten ways, so each clone's influence drops super-linearly — a botnet pays quadratically for the sway one identity earns linearly. Cheap registration stays an oasis for tourists, but no haven for attackers, because every wallet must anchor real stake for real time before its voice counts.
